subject: MAP: Hosting & regional compliance — proposed evaluation runbook
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehra <asha@helix.health>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Hosting & regional compliance — proposed evaluation runbook

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the time today — good to hear more about Helix Health's timelines and the compliance constraints for your patient-facing products. Per our conversation I put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) and an evaluation runbook that tries to cover the three deployment lanes we discussed (Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private/VPC).

High-level ask from you: confirm whether data residency within US-only cloud regions and SOC2 evidence are gating items for go/no-go or preference-level items for the initial PoC. That will determine the MAP path (hosted + geofence vs dedicated/reserved vs private on-prem).

Attached: MAP-Helix-20261117.xlsx — timeline, owners, criteria for go/no-go, and acceptance tests. Also attached a SOC2 snapshot for our hosted controls.

Proposed next steps (short):
- You: call out "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" by 11/12 EOD (data residency, E2E audit logs, encryption at rest KMS linkage)
- We: internal sizing + quick cost delta table for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private by 11/15
- Joint: 60-min alignment meeting week of 11/16 to lock the MAP and schedule the PoC (if aligned)

If it helps, I can run through the acceptance criteria in the attached sheet on our call.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-Helix-20261117.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2-snapshot-2026Q3.pdf (pdf)
From: Asha Mehra <asha@helix.health>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@helix.health>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: Hosting & regional compliance — proposed evaluation runbook

Connor —

Appreciate the summary and the MAP draft. A few clarifying points from our side before we lock dates:  

1) Data residency: "Must-have" for PHI that originates in the US. We cannot have backups or logs stored in other regions for that dataset.
2) SOC2: We require current SOC2 Type II evidence for any hosted environment, and evidence that logs/audit trails are exportable to our SIEM.
3) Private deployment: our infra team wants a cost/time-to-deliver estimate — if private/on-prem is >12 weeks we may instead accept dedicated in a single US region as an interim.

Can you call out what changes in the acceptance tests between the three lanes (particularly around audit/log export and KMS integration)? Also please add our security contact (I copied Procurement; I'll forward the security contact once Procurement okays the nda).

Best,
Asha Mehra
Head of Product Ops, Helix Health

Subject: Fwd: MAP: Hosting & regional compliance — Helix asks and proposed internal runbook

Team — forwarding Asha's notes (see below). Key asks: US-only residency for PHI, SOC2 evidence for hosted, log export to their SIEM, and a private/on-prem timeline vs Dedicated as an interim.

My proposed internal plan:
- 11/12: Product/security quick sync to confirm what we can document as "hosted controls" for SOC2 export and KMS integrations (owner: Laura)
- 11/15: Cost delta and ETA for Dedicated pool vs Private (owner: Karthik) — include ramp/reservation options and lead times for on-prem package
- 11/16: Customer alignment call (60m) to pick lane and sign MAP; include Solutions + Infra + Security

Acceptance test delta (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-live; requires us to provide documented SOC2 evidence and a statement of data residency policy (can offer US-only geofence, backups still need confirmation). Audit/export: provide SIEM-compatible syslog/streaming audit pipe (contracted add-on).
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pool in a single US region; full KMS key wrapping with customer CMK possible via HSM/KMS integration; audit logs retained per agreement; SLA on latency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer network control and air-gapped options; longer lead time (estimate 8-14 weeks) and separate licensing model.

Attachments: MAP-Helix-20261117.xlsx (owner: Connor) — I'll update the acceptance-tests tab once Laura confirms items.

Any objections or additions?

Connor
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehra <asha@helix.health>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Final MAP proposal & timeboxed eval plan — Helix Health

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the quick clarification earlier this week. We've updated the MAP and acceptance tests to reflect your must-haves (US-only for PHI, explicit audit export path, SOC2 artifacts). Summary and asks below — full MAP in the attached sheet and in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bHelix-MAP

Summary (short):
- Recommended initial lane: Dedicated pool in US region (Minneapolis) as the balance of speed, residency, and KMS flexibility. This satisfies PHI residency and gives you an intermediate with customer-key option.
- Private/on-prem remains an option if you need air-gap or on-prem KMS, ETA ~10 weeks after order approval.
- Hosted (our standard public API) is possible only if we contract the US-only geofence add-on plus an addendum on backup handling — otherwise it does not meet your "must-have" for backups.

Proposed timeboxed eval plan (week-level):
- Week 1 (11/18): Kickoff — confirm lane (dedicated vs private) and sign MAP/nda; infra/Security onboarding
- Week 2 (11/25): Dedicated pool provisioning (or private delivery slot allocation) & KMS integration test (customer CMK staging)
- Week 3 (12/02): Acceptance test run — audit log export to Helix SIEM, throughput/latency smoke tests, and failure/fallback exercise
- Week 4 (12/09): Close decision window and plan go/no-go for PoC -> production pilot

Requested actions from Helix:
1) Confirm lane preference (Dedicated or Private) by 11/18 EOD
2) Share security contact + SOC2 acceptance checklist (Procurement can forward)

I've attached the updated MAP and SOC2 snapshot. Also added a HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/48392 so Procurement and legal can reference the paperwork.

If that schedule works, I'll book the 60m alignment call for 11/18 (10am PT) with infra and security on our side — please let me know if a different slot is better.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-Helix-20261117.xlsx, SOC2-snapshot-2026Q3.pdf
